title: Human lung organoid modelling of tissue-resident antiviral T cell responses
title_zh: 人类肺器官模型中组织驻留抗病毒T细胞反应的建模
abstract: Tissue-resident immunity constitutes a first line of defence against pathogens and enables rapid innate and adaptive memory responses1–3. However, experimental studies have been hindered by a lack of holistic human in vitro models that enable epithelial infection in the context of tissue-resident immune subsets. In lung, differing notions of transient versus sustained residency of tissue-resident memory T cells (TRM cells) have challenged the extent to which anamnestic recall immunity to respiratory pathogens occurs locally or in concert with secondary lymphoid organs4–6. Here we generated long-term adult human distal lung organoids from intact tissue fragments in 3D air–liquid interface culture, which co-preserved epithelial and stromal components with endogenous lung-resident immune cells (T cells, B cells, natural killer cells and myeloid cells). The organoid T cells expressed residency and memory markers and preserved T cell receptor repertoires of cognate fresh tissue. SARS-CoV-2 infected the organoid lung epithelium, stimulated inflammatory cytokine production and, crucially, induced SARS-CoV-2-specific, tissue-resident T cell responses. Furthermore, boosting T cells within intact organoids with SARS-CoV-2 peptide pools blunted subsequent SARS-CoV-2 infection, consistent with a component of virus-specific protective TRM cell function in the absence of secondary lymphoid tissues. Overall, this immunocompetent lung organoid system demonstrates functional control of viral infection by lung-intrinsic memory T cell responses, provides a rationale for local vaccination strategies and validates a general platform for investigation of human tissue-resident immunity in health and disease. Lung organoids containing endogenous resident immune cells show that SARS-CoV-2 infection elicits protective, tissue-resident memory T cell responses, demonstrating local recall immunity and providing a platform for the study of human tissue-resident antiviral defence.
abstract_zh: 组织驻留免疫是病原体的第一道防线，并能启动快速的固有和适应性记忆反应1–3。然而，由于缺乏能够在组织驻留免疫亚群背景下实现上皮感染的整体人体体外模型，实验研究一直受到阻碍。在肺中，组织驻留记忆T细胞（TRM细胞）短暂与持续驻留的不同概念挑战了呼吸道病原体局部或与次级淋巴器官协同诱导回忆免疫的程度4–6。本研究通过3D气液界面培养从完整组织碎片中建立了长期成年人类远端肺器官，该模型保留了上皮和基质成分以及内源性肺组织驻留免疫细胞（T细胞、B细胞、自然杀伤细胞和髓系细胞）。器官中的T细胞表达驻留和记忆标记物，并保留了新鲜组织中T细胞受体（TCR）的特异性谱系。SARS-CoV-2感染器官肺上皮，诱导炎症细胞因子产生，并关键地诱导了SARS-CoV-2特异性的组织驻留T细胞反应。此外，在完整器官中用SARS-CoV-2肽池增强T细胞，随后挑战SARS-CoV-2感染，抑制了感染，这与在次级淋巴组织之外的病毒特异性驻留记忆T细胞功能的组成部分一致。总体而言，该免疫 competent 肺器官系统展示了肺内源性记忆T细胞反应对病毒感染的功能控制，为局部疫苗策略提供了依据，并验证了研究人类组织驻留免疫在健康和疾病中的通用平台。含内源性驻留免疫细胞的肺器官显示，SARS-CoV-2感染诱导了保护性的组织驻留记忆T细胞反应，展示了局部回忆免疫，并为研究人类组织驻留抗病毒防御提供了平台。
